correctness.rationale: For n≥2 and 1≤w≤n, H_n(x) is the unweighted mean-centered Euclidean seminorm and M_{n,w} is cyclic contiguous forward-window max. On a strict-selector chamber, the map copies input coordinates with multiplicities c_j≤w and its unique global maximum has c_p=w. For 2w≤n, output-centered energy ≤Σ c_j(h_j−mean h)^2≤wH_n(h)^2. For 2w>n, writing R=max h−min h and using convexity of centered copying energy on the coordinate box reduces the worst case to binary endpoints; since one multiplicity is w>n/2, binary copied count t lies in [0,n−w]∪[w,n], hence output H²≤w(n−w)R²/n. Input H²≥R²/2 by the two extreme coordinates. Thus L²≤2w(n−w)/n. A two-site peak baseline p=0,q=w for short windows and q=n−w for long windows has disjoint winning patterns; perturb ε(e_p−e_q) to attain equality in both branches. For w=n output is constant and L=0, for w=1 identity L=1. Continuity over finitely many affine chamber transitions upgrades a branch bound to arbitrary pairs, even with ties. Independent exact two-peak calculations at n=5,7,9,12 corroborate squared factors and equality; not proof for all n.
